To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) root proliferation rate (i.e. the rate at which the root number increased after the first root appeared) differed greatly between crops, and (b) root front velocity (the speed at which the root front moved down in the soil) also differed greatly between crops.

(a) the velocity of the rooting front after planting differs greatly between crops, (b) the velocity of rooting is not related to the root proliferation rate, (c) root proliferation rate and depth of rooting are related and (d) the relationship between thermal time and root proliferation is linear.

the rooting depth, root proliferation rate and velocity of the root growth front after planting are crop specific, and that the root proliferation rate and the velocity of the growth front after planting do not correlate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of rooting characteristics of crops in relation to thermal time and the velocity of the rooting front.
the development of a method to assess rooting behaviour of crops in a quantitative manner and to compare crops on the basis of rooting characteristics.
the development of rooting characteristics in a wide range of crops, and we present data for 14 crops that were grown in a controlled environment at Wageningen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
root growth is a crop specific process, but that it is possible to establish general relationships between rooting depth, root proliferation and the velocity of the growing root front.
there is no single relationship between thermal time after planting, rooting depth, velocity of the root fronts or root proliferation.
the velocity of the rooting front of a crop and the rooting depth are determined by the crop itself and not by the environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
root characteristics of crops are highly variable and that this variability can be described in a quantitative way by the two parameters mentioned above.
the root proliferation rate is a better parameter than the velocity of the ‘root front’ for comparing crops.
the root proliferation rate is a crop characteristic, while the root front velocity is a crop characteristic modified by environmental factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to predict root development of crops in terms of rooting depth and root proliferation rate.
it provides a simple method for comparing root growth between crops and that the method is applicable to crops that are not normally studied in rhizotrons.
the root proliferation rate is a useful crop parameter for describing root growth.
